concepts.label: te-node
concepts.gloss: A TE node is a network element (a vertex in a TE/topology layer) that hosts termination points, switching state and per-node TE information and is a part of a particular TE topology.
concepts.example: R1 — the TE node R1 represents the router/OTN element at site R1 that lives inside the OTN layer topology and hosts TPs (e.g., tp-R1-R2), a connectivity matrix and node TLVs.

concepts.label: termination-point
concepts.gloss: A termination point is a node-local interface/port object that terminates a TE link and identifies where that link attaches to a TE node.
concepts.example: tp-R1-R2 — the termination point on node R1 that terminates the TE link to R2 (it is the R1 end of telink-R1-R2).

concepts.label: supporting-tp
concepts.gloss: A supporting termination (supporting-tp) is an adaptation mapping that records that a higher‑layer termination point is realized/supported by a lower‑layer termination point (an adaptation relationship between layers on the same node).
concepts.example: ODU tp over OTU tp at R2 — the ODU-layer TP at R2 is realised by (supported by) a specific OTU-layer TP on the same node.
instances: OTN tp over optical tp at R1
ODU tp over OTU tp at R2

concepts.label: tunnel-termination-point
concepts.gloss: A tunnel‑termination‑point (TTP) is a logical termination on a TE node that serves as the head/tail (origin or destination) of a TE tunnel and is bound to that node.
concepts.example: ttp-A1 (tunnel head) — the TTP on node A1 that originates the TE tunnel whose traffic enters the network at A1.

concepts.label: te-tunnel
concepts.gloss: A TE tunnel is an end‑to‑end traffic‑engineered service/path that originates at one or more TTPs, is routed over a specific TE topology, and may be associated with protection (a protection group).
concepts.example: tunnel-a1a3-odu2 (ODU2, A1-A3, protected) — an ODU2 tunnel from A1 to A3 routed over the OTN topology and protected by pgroup-a1a3.

concepts.label: otn-label
concepts.gloss: An OTN label (tributary‑slot / TS/TPN) identifies the specific tributary slot or time‑position within a higher‑order OTN container that is allocated to carry a tunnel's payload.
concepts.example: TS/TPN for ODU2 in OTU4 — the particular tributary slot inside an OTU4 frame reserved to carry an ODU2 tunnel.

concepts.label: connectivity-matrix
concepts.gloss: A connectivity matrix is a node‑local switching description that specifies how input termination points map to output termination points through the node's switching fabric (used to represent cross‑connects or forwarding capabilities).
concepts.example: R2 connectivity matrix — the listing on node R2 that shows which incoming TPs are connected to which outgoing TPs for ODU/optical switching at R2.

concepts.label: te-link
concepts.gloss: A TE link is an adjacency (physical or logical) between two TE nodes, represented by link endpoints (termination points) on the two nodes.
concepts.example: telink-R1-R2 — the TE link connecting node R1 and node R2, terminated by the termination points at those nodes (e.g., tp-R1-R2 and the corresponding tp-R2-R1).

concepts.label: te-topology
concepts.gloss: A TE topology is the per‑layer network graph (the network view for a layer) that contains the TE nodes and TE links over which TE services are established.
concepts.example: the OTN layer network — the TE topology for the OTN layer that contains nodes R1..Rn and links such as telink-R1-R2 used to route ODU tunnels.

concepts.label: tunnel-connection-endpoint
concepts.gloss: A tunnel‑connection‑endpoint (TCEP) is the node‑specific endpoint instance of a particular tunnel, representing that tunnel's attachment/endpoint state on a given node.
concepts.example: tcep-a1a3-R1 — the TCEP object at node R1 that represents the endpoint of tunnel-a1a3 on R1 (the tunnel’s ingress/egress representation at that node).

concepts.label: wson-optical-channel
concepts.gloss: An optical channel (OCh) is a wavelength/lambda channel in a WSON context that carries client signals between nodes and is realized over an optical multiplex section.
concepts.example: och-lambda1-R1-R3 — the optical channel using wavelength lambda1 between R1 and R3 that is carried over the underlying OMS spans.

concepts.label: optical-multiplex-section
concepts.gloss: An optical‑multiplex‑section (OMS) is the optical span between two nodes that aggregates multiple optical channels (wavelengths) and provides the transport medium for those OChs.
concepts.example: oms-R1-R2 — the OMS between R1 and R2 that aggregates multiple wavelengths (e.g., och-lambda1-R1-R2 and och-lambda2-R1-R2).

concepts.label: service-grade
concepts.gloss: A service‑grade is the class or tier assigned to a tunnel that expresses its relative priority or SLA treatment within the TE domain.
concepts.example: gold for tunnel-a1a3-odu2 — tunnel-a1a3-odu2 has been assigned the 'gold' service grade indicating a higher priority SLA.

concepts.label: protection-group
concepts.gloss: A protection‑group groups one or more paths/tunnels into a protection arrangement (e.g., 1+1), defining how traffic is protected and which alternate paths exist.
concepts.example: pgroup-a1a3 (1+1) — a 1+1 protection group protecting the A1–A3 tunnel, providing a working path and a separate protect path for automatic switch-over.

concepts.label: protection-role
concepts.gloss: A protection‑role is the role assigned to a path within a protection group (for example 'working' or 'protect'), identifying which route is active and which is standby.
concepts.example: working = R1-R3 and protect = R1-R4-R3 — within pgroup-a1a3 the working role uses R1–R3 while the protect role uses R1–R4–R3 as the standby path.

concepts.label: ext-tlv-42
concepts.gloss: ext‑tlv‑42 is an opaque, node‑attached TLV (extension) used to carry vendor‑specific or auxiliary data in a node's TE advertisement or configuration.
concepts.example: ext-tlv-42=0x77 on R2 — node R2 advertises/contains opaque extension TLV number 42 with value 0x77 attached to its TE state.
